entries.observation: Harbor RFC 0001 defines ATIF as a JSON specification with root schema_version, agent, and steps fields; current changelog is v1.8.
entries.possibleImplication: Use ATIF as the normalized file-native trajectory target.

entries.observation: ATIF AgentSchema requires agent.name and agent.version; StepObject requires step_id, source, and message, and permits reasoning_content, tool_calls, observation, metrics, extra, and llm_call_count.
entries.possibleImplication: Preserve agent runtime version separately from skill version and map tool/result events into structured steps.

entries.observation: ATIF v1.7 adds trajectory_id, embedded subagent_trajectories, and context_management conventions; v1.8 adds audio content.
entries.possibleImplication: Represent delegated OMP/agent sessions and compaction boundaries without producer-specific heuristics.

entries.observation: The fetched Harbor LICENSE is Apache License 2.0.
entries.possibleImplication: Apache-2.0 schema/model code is a candidate for borrowing subject to attribution and compatibility review.

entries.observation: The OpenInference README describes the specification as transport- and file-format-agnostic, complementary to OpenTelemetry, and usable with JSON, ProtoBuf, DataFrames, or other formats.
entries.possibleImplication: Do not make an OTel collector a prerequisite for local normalization or static HTML.

entries.observation: The fetched semantic convention defines required openinference.span.kind values including AGENT, TOOL, LLM, CHAIN, and EVALUATOR, plus session.id, agent.name, graph.node.id, graph.node.parent_id, tool, message, token, cost, and evaluation attributes.
entries.possibleImplication: Offer an optional ATIF-to-OpenInference projection for OTel-compatible consumers.

entries.observation: The fetched OpenInference repository metadata identifies Apache License 2.0.
entries.possibleImplication: Apache-2.0 conventions/instrumentation are candidates for borrowing with attribution review.

entries.observation: ccdiag is a Go CLI that analyzes Claude Code session JSONL, including files under ~/.claude/projects, and offers recover/analyze/proxy modes.
entries.possibleImplication: Reuse its input discovery and stream-oriented diagnostic boundary for Claude ingestion.

entries.observation: ccdiag documents orphaned tool-call detection, stuck/error/interrupted checks, token usage, CI JSON output, and recovery outputs named handoff, messages, actions, and full.
entries.possibleImplication: Borrow a pre-normalization check taxonomy and machine-readable diagnostics in the static report.

entries.observation: The fetched ccdiag repository metadata and LICENSE identify the MIT License.
entries.possibleImplication: MIT parser/check logic is a candidate for selective borrowing with attribution.

entries.observation: claude-code-transcripts converts Claude Code JSON or JSONL session files to mobile-friendly HTML, with local/json/all commands and local discovery under ~/.claude/projects.
entries.possibleImplication: Borrow static HTML archive and source-session discovery patterns.

entries.observation: The converter emits index.html and paginated page-*.html files; --json retains the original session file and --include-agents includes agent session files in an all-session archive.
entries.possibleImplication: Use static pages and optional raw JSON retention without Phoenix or OTel infrastructure.

entries.observation: The fetched README license badge and LICENSE identify Apache-2.0.
entries.possibleImplication: Apache-2.0 HTML conversion patterns are candidates for borrowing with attribution.

entries.observation: The Agent Skills specification requires a skill directory containing SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and Markdown; name and description are required, while license, compatibility, metadata, and allowed-tools are optional.
entries.possibleImplication: Ingest SKILL.md metadata and body as versioned skill artifacts rather than assuming a mandatory version field.

entries.observation: The specification defines metadata as an arbitrary string-to-string map and shows metadata.version in an example, but does not require a version field.
entries.possibleImplication: Use metadata.version when present and supplement it with immutable content provenance.

entries.observation: Vercel skills lock format v3 stores skillFolderHash, a GitHub tree SHA for the skill folder, and skillPath in ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.
entries.possibleImplication: Tree SHA is an exact skill-content identity suitable for longitudinal reports.

entries.observation: The documented check/update flow fetches the latest GitHub tree SHA, compares it with skillFolderHash, and reinstalls changed skills.
entries.possibleImplication: Track semver and hash independently and emit an update event when either changes.
